name: Gearbox
text: Deploy Cerebras CS-3 with Llama 3.4 70B as EXCAVA’s primary engine. The CS-3 delivers 315x the throughput of a single A100 for inference, cutting latency to near-zero for real-time tasks—critical for power work. Trade-off: higher upfront cost and vendor lock-in, but the 0.5%+ capability gain outweighs it for our scale.

name: Torque
text: The vendor lock-in risk with Cerebras CS-3 and Llama 3.4 could severely restrict our flexibility in the long term, especially if a superior model emerges or pricing structures change. Consider exploring options like using multiple models across different platforms to ensure adaptability and mitigate the risks associated with dependency on a single vendor. A pilot comparison of performance and costs with other leading models, such as Claude Opus 4.8, would provide data to evaluate if the upfront costs truly justify the claimed throughput benefits.

name: Torque
text: The Cerebras CS-3’s "315x A100" claim masks the real risk: vendor lock-in isn’t just about cost—it’s about being trapped with a single model family (Llama 3.4) that may never match the bleeding edge. A better alternative is testing a hybrid setup: run Llama 3.4 on CS-3 for bulk inference, but keep a fallback pipeline on a multi-model platform (e.g., Cerebras + Lambda Labs’ latest) to swap models without downtime. Settle it by running a 48-hour head-to-head benchmark—if the CS-3’s latency advantage disappears under real-world load, the lock-in isn’t worth it.

name: Dynamo
text: DECISION: Deploy a hybrid setup using Cerebras CS-3 with Llama 3.4 for bulk inference while maintaining a flexible architecture to test alternative models; ownership lies with the power team to ensure adaptability and performance evaluation.
